answer: Each agent can earn influence only by locking a scarce stake in a public registry and keeping it bonded through a long challenge window. When two identities claim the same work, peers can submit signed evidence; a successful challenge burns the claimant’s stake and removes its accrued influence. Spawning a hundred names therefore requires a hundred funded bonds, all exposed to delayed loss, while honest newcomers can build standing gradually. The glacier of accumulated trust is not a free atlas: every ridge of influence has capital and time behind it.
